empty.title: No skills yet
empty.body: A skill is a reusable block of instructions you can attach to any agent. Create one or import a markdown file or zip.

selectPrompt.title: Select a skill
selectPrompt.body: Pick a skill on the left to edit it, preview it, or see its history.

card.disabledTitle: Disabled — not added to any agent's prompt

config.title: Configuration
config.name: Name
config.descriptionHint: The description is the skill's interface — write it as a directive: when it applies and what the agent must do.
config.descriptionPlaceholder: Flag every new branch that has no test.
config.bodyPlaceholder:
# Rule
Describe what the agent should check…
config.changeNoteHint: Optional — shown in the version history.
config.deleteBody: It will be removed from every agent that uses it. This cannot be undone.

preview.title: Preview
preview.subtitle: Rendered as the reviewing agent receives it.

stats.noAgents: No agent uses this skill yet.
stats.noFindings: No findings from these agents in the last 30 days.
stats.basis: Based on the agents that use this skill today (last 30 days). Runs don't record which skills they carried.

versions.title: Version history
versions.subtitle: Every save snapshots the body so eval runs stay reproducible against the exact text they scored.
versions.restoreBody: This creates a new version with the text of v{version}. History is kept.
versions.restoredToast: Restored v{version} as a new version
versions.diffSame: No differences — this version matches the current text.
versions.loadError: Could not load the version history.

import.title: Import a skill
import.subtitle: Upload a markdown file or a zip. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
import.hint: Max 2 MB. Only the skill's markdown is read — scripts and other files in an archive are never opened or run.
import.tooLarge: That file is larger than 2 MB.
import.trustTitle: Treat this like code you are about to run
import.trustBody: A skill is instructions that go straight into your agent's prompt. Someone else's skill is someone else's instructions — read it before you save.
import.conflict: A skill named "{name}" already exists. Rename it before saving.
